text:
Alice Walker: Quick sync — we need to finalize span naming + semantic attrs for inference spans (model calls). I sketched a pattern, want feedback before I update the otel pipeline docs.

Ben Chu: 👍 send the sketch. main concerns: cardinality, PII, and what goes into span.name vs attributes.

Alice Walker: sketch: span.name = "inference.{op}" or "inference.{model_family}.{op}"? e.g. `inference.t5.generate` or `inference.generate`. keep name short for dashboards. put specific model id/version in attributes.

Carol Singh: prefer `inference.{op}` as the canonical span name. otherwise we explode dashboards across models. model details belong in attributes: `redwood.model.id`, `redwood.model.version` (string), and `redwood.model.variant` (quantized/8bit etc).

Dave R.: +1 on name minimalism. also add `redwood.inference.family` as a normalized enum (t5, llama, gpt, custom) to allow grouping without freeform model ids.

Emily (eng-platform): question: model.version has high cardinality (commit hashes / long strings). can we canonicalize? maybe `redwood.model.version_major` or map to release tags.

Ben Chu: for now let's store both: `redwood.model.version` but hashed (sha256 prefix) and `redwood.model.version_tag` (stable tag or semver) if available. hashed version is safe for internal correlation but not human-friendly.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: do NOT include prompt text or any user-provided content in span attributes. Redact/omit all PII.

Carol Singh: attributes I propose (low-cardinality when possible):
- `span.name`: "inference.generate" or "inference.embed"
- `redwood.inference.family`: enum (t5, llama, gpt, custom)
- `redwood.model.id`: normalized id (e.g., llama-2-13b)
- `redwood.model.version_tag`: stable release tag if available
- `redwood.model.version_hash`: short hash (6 chars) for correlation
- `redwood.model.variant`: enum (fp16, int8, q4_0)
- `redwood.inference.tokens_in`: bucketed ("<16", "16-64", "64-256", "256+")
- `redwood.inference.tokens_out`: bucketed same as above
- `redwood.kv_cache.hits`: integer? maybe bucketed (`0`, `1-5`, `5+`) to avoid high-cardinality
- `redwood.kv_cache.partial_hit`: boolean
- `redwood.quality.eval_set`: if request was part of an eval, use eval id but limited set (only internal)
- `redwood.route.policy`: enum (latency, cost, region-fallback)

Dave R.: bucket tokens is smart. numeric token counts will blow up metrics. use histogram metrics for token distribution but attributes should be buckets.

Emily (eng-platform): for exporters: internal OTLP -> bigquery should capture full attrs (including version_hash). External dashboards (datadog/newrelic) should ingest a sanitized set: family, id (no hash), tokens buckets, cache_hit boolean, route policy. Also implement exporter filters to drop high-card attrs for external exporters.

Ben Chu: agree. here's a rough otel processor snippet we can add to pipeline (pseudoconfig):
```
processors:
  attribute/normalize:
    actions:
      - key: redwood.model.version_hash
        action: hash
      - key: user.id
        action: delete
  exporter/filter_external:
    include: ["redwood.inference.family","redwood.model.id","redwood.inference.tokens_in","redwood.inference.tokens_out","redwood.kv_cache.partial_hit","redwood.route.policy"]
    exclude: ["redwood.model.version_hash","redwood.model.version_tag","redwood.quality.eval_set"]
```

Carol Singh: we should also standardize span status codes for inference semantics: `OK`, `ERROR_MODEL_TIMEOUT`, `ERROR_QUOTA`, `ERROR_INTERNAL`. map to OpenTelemetry status + add `redwood.error.code` attr for machine-readable reasons.

Alice Walker: rollout UX question — when we roll a new model, dashboards should be able to show comparisons. if we keep span.name the same and tag model via `redwood.model.version_tag`, we can do per-version slicing easily. good.

Ops Sam: retention policy: internal bigquery raw traces keep 90 days. aggregated metrics/dashboards keep 1 year. external exporters should have shorter retention. confirm with security if version_hash or model_id are considered sensitive.

Emily (eng-platform): note: cardinality guardrails: max 50 unique values per attribute for metrics/backends that warn on high-card. enforce via processor that maps unknown model ids to `other` after threshold.

Ben Chu: final ask: please add a short section in the observability README with examples of span queries to generate the model comparison dashboard (filter by `redwood.model.version_tag`). I'll draft after we agree on attr names.

Alice Walker: action items:
- Carol: write up final attr list and bucket boundaries (tokens & kv cache) — due EOD today
- Emily: add exporter filters and retention notes to otel pipeline PR — due tomorrow
- Ben: draft dashboard query examples once attrs are final
- Dave: add unit tests for attr normalization/transforms in telemetry repo

telemetry-bot: Noted: new thread label `telemetry/span-naming-inference` created.

Carol Singh: pinging here with one more caveat — do not use freeform route ids in spans. always map route to `redwood.route.policy` + `redwood.route.bucket` (regional/cost).

Alice Walker: thanks all. I'll wait for Carol's writeup and then merge the doc to `docs/otel-inference.md`. :thumbsup:
